source_caption:
In ‘The Passion of the Christ’ (2004), there is a creepy scene where Satan is shown holding a strange, adult-looking baby while Jesus is being whipped.

Mel Gibson said the scene was meant to be a dark version of the Madonna and Child, meant to mock purity and innocence.

While the Virgin Mary watches her Son being tortured, Satan copies her by carrying a demonic child through the crowd.

The scene suggests that Satan, who represents evil, appears to care for his child, while God seems to have left His Son to suffer alone.

Mel Gibson struggled to get Hollywood studios to back his film. Many studios were reluctant because it focused on the crucifixion of Jesus, used Aramaic and Latin with subtitles, and was considered a risky and controversial project. Because of this, Mel Gibson decided to finance the movie himself, investing about $30 million through his company Icon Productions.

Despite the lack of traditional studio backing, the film went on to become a massive success. Distributed in the United States by Newmarket Films, it earned more than $600 million worldwide, making it one of the most successful independent films ever and the highest-grossing Christian film in history.

source_details.synopsis: The Passion of the Christ is a 2004 American epic biblical drama film co-produced and directed by Mel Gibson from a screenplay he wrote with Benedict Fitzgerald. It is the first installment of The Passion of the Christ film series. The film stars Jim Caviezel as Jesus, Maia Morgenstern as his mother Mary, and Monica Bellucci as Mary Magdalene. It depicts the arrest, trial and crucifixion of Jesus, largely according to the canonical gospels as well as additional accounts such as the purported mystical visions by Anne Catherine Emmerich and the Friday of Sorrows.
